previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with acute chest pain and shortness of breath during a dialysis session. Evaluation revealed mild troponin elevation without EKG changes, hypertension, and signs of fluid overload including pulmonary edema on imaging. Symptoms were attributed to demand ischemia secondary to hypervolemia. Ultrafiltration removed 4.1 liters of fluid, leading to resolution of symptoms and improvement in vital signs and labs. She remained stable throughout the hospital stay with controlled blood pressure, improved respiratory status, and no further cardiac events. She was discharged to an extended care facility with instructions for strict fluid and salt restriction, daily weight monitoring, and continuation of home medications with adjustments to sevelamer and insulin dosing.
